raw.body:
# ARENA — one tracker for the whole page

**Consolidated 2026-10-23 on the owner's instruction: related issues on one page belong in ONE tracker with checkboxes, not scattered across many.** Each line below was its own issue; the originals are closed and stay readable for detail. **Nothing is lost — only the count.**

## Open work

- [ ] **[PM 2026-11-08] Needs a shared-DB write for the `lhq_labels` rows, so it's owner-gated; it can't close from a PR alone.** **The advice strip is incomplete beyond `lib/patterns.ts`** - `lib/labelDefaults.en.json:1317` `HOURS_WIN_MON_EVE_DESC` is live on `/hours` and reads "Strong trend continuation or violent reversal setups": the same prediction-with-no-evidence class as "breakout pending". It is a label key, so 4 locales plus `lhq_labels`, and the database half is owner-gated. *(QA 2026-11-08 - MY scoping error: I filed the advice problem as a one-file problem)*

- [x] **[PM audit 2026-11-08, Dev evidence comment of 00:09Z; PM spot-read main]** DONE, live on main: `detectPatterns` returns `rankPatterns(found)`, Double top/bottom rank first and Tight consolidation last; all 8 emitted names match RANK. **`lib/patterns.ts`: ONE IN FOUR ALERTS HIDES A REVERSAL BEHIND A COMPRESSION LABEL** — the alert shows `pats[0]`, which is source-code check order, not significance. **Measured on live data: 63 of 196 windows (32.1%) contain a Double top or Double bottom, and 51 of them (26.0% of ALL windows) have it not-first, so the user never sees it.** The masker is almost always `Tight consolidation (compression - breakout pending)`, pushed at check 5 while double top is appended at check 6. *(QA 2026-11-08 — the highest-impact of the three)*
- [x] **[PM audit 2026-11-08] DONE, in a different form than `>`:** the steps keep `>=` deliberately (equal highs are ordinary), and the predicate requires strict net progress (`roseNet`/`fellNet`: `highs10[last] > highs10[0] && lows10[last] > lows10[0]`), so a flat series can't be called an uptrend. Dev's retraction: comment 6714911852. **`lib/patterns.ts`: a flat market satisfies the uptrend test** — both trend tests use `>=`, so ten identical candles pass both. **Hygiene, not live: measured 0 of 196 windows, and NO trend name fired at all** — `every()` over 10 bars needs a monotonic run that real candles rarely produce. **Caveat: that was one snapshot across 49 coins x 4 intervals, not sampling over time, so it bounds how COMMON this is and does not establish the branch is unreachable.** Do not delete the trend block on the strength of it without sampling across days. *(QA 2026-11-08, pinned by 11 cells)*
- [x] **[PM audit 2026-11-08, Dev evidence comment of 00:09Z; PM spot-read main]** DONE, live on main: the unreachable ratio is removed and survives only in the comment explaining why. **`lib/patterns.ts`: `cr >= pr * 0.8` is unreachable** — the preceding engulfing conditions force `cr >= pr` arithmetically. Reads as a tunable threshold and is not one. *(QA 2026-11-08)*

- [x] **[PM audit 2026-11-08, Dev evidence comment of 00:09Z; PM spot-read main]** DONE, live on main: Arena seeding waits for settingsLoadStatus 'ready' (and won't seed from defaults on 'error', #1347), covering all four persisted values. StrategyPanel has no storage of its own. **Saved selections vs settings load** — the Arena and Strategy Panel read saved selections before settings have loaded, so a user's choice can be overwritten by defaults. *(this issue's original subject)*
- [x] *(PM 2026-11-13: closed. Factual half 3a46aae2, redesign #2162/#2184; "Recommended preset" dropped, nothing ever backed it, comment 6857455030.)* **[PM 2026-11-08] FACTUAL HALF ALREADY DONE (3a46aae2, 2026-09-07, PM's #967 ruling): all 21 chips stay; the 12 that can't draw are dimmed with "not available yet" in their accessible name and refuse selection (`components/StrategyPanel.tsx:239, 365-373`). Remaining: `describeSelection` gets a canRender filter so a pre-2026-09-07 saved id never reaches the AI prompt (0 prod rows today; Dev). The three DESIGN halves (Free/Pro limit, selected state, Recommended preset) are LATER, PM's call.** **Strategy panel honesty** — show only indicators that actually work, a clear Free/Pro limit, an obvious selected state, and a Recommended preset. *(was #1601)*
- [x] **[PM audit 2026-11-08] NOT REPRODUCED (QA, rendered on qa):** clicking a category visibly swaps the gold highlight from All to the chosen chip (computed colour, background and border), screenshots in qa/.shots-1263. The adjacent accessibility gap is real and is its own box below. **Coin category gives no visible feedback** — picking a category changes nothing on screen until the coin list is opened. *(was #1603)*
- [x] **[PM 2026-11-15: all three halves shipped. Empty answer: 2f72cde4 (#1583), in v2026.10.21; stale signal: 40c06fb1, bars-ago age + amber past 50 bars, on main; cold-load: v2026.10.28. Dev re-checked on current dev, PM verified both commits are ancestors of main.]** **Empty AI answer breaks the page** — plus a stale “latest signal” and a cold-load “Signal unavailable”. *(was #1583, from #1541 QA)* **ONE OF THE THREE IS FIXED AND SHIPPED — the cold-load “Signal unavailable”, in `v2026.10.28`.** `lib/venueFallback.ts` is on `main` and `useEMAStrategy.ts` now calls `firstVenueThatAnswers` across Bybit then Binance futures. The old code returned on the first line and **threw** on failure, so the Binance line ran only for coins Bybit does not list — the one case where it is not a fallback — and for the 44 coins on both venues a Bybit 502 printed “Signal unavailable right now” with a working source one unreached line below. **That is the intermittent failure the owner reported.** **NOT ticking this item, because the empty-AI-answer and stale-latest-signal halves are untouched.** The reported symptom stopping is not the item being done, and ticking on the owner's symptom is how the other two halves get lost. **Reader beware:** the broken `if (bySym) return fetchBybitKlines(...)` is still in `useEMAStrategy.ts` around line 170, **inside the comment documenting what it used to be** — a grep finds it and reports the bug as live. See [[reference_grep_matches_comment_prose]].
- [x] **[PM 2026-11-08] DECIDED: NO for now.** 50 coins is enough before there are users, and widening 50 to 463 multiplies the per-coin fan-out cost about ninefold (`app/(main)/arena/page.tsx:123`). Revisit when paying users ask for specific coins. **More coins** — Arena offers 50; Bybit lists 798 and Binance 524 USDT perps. Decide the real ceiling and the selection rule. *(was #1600)*
- [x] **[PM audit 2026-11-08, Dev evidence comment of 00:09Z; PM spot-read main]** DONE, live on main: distinct BAD_ANSWER and UNDRAWABLE codes (PM read 2 non-comment UNDRAWABLE lines on main), no bare empty structures. Draw Structure's column IS on prod (PM measured draw_structure_count present, 11-08), so it's enabled there. **Draw Structure answers "Nothing proposed on this window." for three different things, two of which are failures.** `app/api/draw-structure/route.ts` returns **200 with `structures: []`** when (a) the model genuinely proposed nothing — the real answer; (b) `toDrawable` dropped **every** proposal as undrawable (`:294-296`); or (c) `parseProposals` found no JSON or `JSON.parse` threw (`:160,166`, both `return []`). The route flattens all three, so (b) and (c) reach the trader as a calm statement about their chart. **Same class as an unreadable AI answer drawn as FLAT, so the same precedent applies** (PM's ruling, 2026-11-05): an unparseable reply becomes an error state, an all-dropped result becomes its own distinct error, and `DRAW_STRUCTURE_NONE` is used **only** for a genuine zero-proposal parse — and the reservation/refund behaviour matches what the other AI routes already do for an unreadable answer, read from them rather than invented. **Sequenced after OKX, but it must land before Draw Structure ships** — the feature is not enabled anywhere yet (`20261031a` unapplied, so it answers `503 NOT_ENABLED`), which is the only reason it can wait. *(found writing the `DRAW_STRUCTURE_NONE` empty state, #1818)*

### On-the-fly indicators audit — carried out of #1347, 2026-10-23

**#1347 was closed with 8 of its boxes unticked, so its remaining work was invisible from here.** QA checked each against current source on 2026-10-23 and they are now boxes of their own. **Five were already fixed and nobody ticked them.** Verdicts are QA's; each still needs PM's rule-8 step-4 audit before it counts as closed.

- [x] **A missing Supabase client no longer leaves the panel loading forever** — `components/SettingsProvider.tsx:300` and `:392` now `setSettingsLoadStatus('error')` instead of the old silent `if (!sb) return;`. *(was #1347 item 8)*
- [x] **The stale-selection check no longer runs before the seed** — three `#1347 item 9` guards in `app/arena/page.tsx` (`:127`, `:293`, `:662`), including the two "we cannot tell" cases that must read as NOT changed. *(was #1347 item 9)*
- [x] **A malformed 200 no longer reports "saved"** — `components/SettingsProvider.tsx:118`: `if (!Array.isArray(body.accepted) || !Array.isArray(body.rejected)) return { failed: true };`, with the reasoning in the comment above it. *(was #1347 item 10)*
- [x] **The alerts copy no longer claims parity** — production's own `/api/labels?locale=en` serves: *"The standard EMA ribbon buy or sell call … **It does not follow your chart's indicator selection, so it can differ from what your chart shows.**"* **This also settles #1347's internal contradiction** — item 14 appeared as `[x]` in its body and `[ ]` in its summary list; the `[x]` was right. *(was #1347 item 14)*
- [x] **The migration's status line is corrected** — `supabase/migrations/20260907a_user_settings_strategy_selection.sql:26` now reads "APPLIED to both" and records that the old "NOT YET APPLIED to either" was false. *(was #1347 item 15)*
- [x] **The NUL byte in `app/arena/page.tsx` is gone** — measured: **0 NUL bytes** in 174,151 bytes / 2,921 lines, so the file greps whole again. It had hidden 56% of the file from every search. *(was #1347's parked #1367)*
- [x] **FIXED, verified 2026-11-11 (Dev):** `!res.ok || cancelled` is live zero times; its only occurrence is the historical comment at `arena/page.tsx:485`. The live code splits it: `:578` `!token || cancelled`, `:591` `if (cancelled) return;` (cancelled is not logged as a failure), and `:597` gates the write. Original: **[PM 2026-11-08] Count corrected (Dev):** `if (!res.ok || cancelled) return;` is live ONCE (`app/(main)/arena/page.tsx:568`); the second grep hit is a comment. Tally: 3 of 7 fixed, 1 present, 3 unverified. **Item 11's remaining collapses — PARTLY fixed, and the remainder is counted rather than guessed.** Of the seven locations #1347 named: `KLineProChart.tsx`'s `indicators ?? []` and `useEMAStrategy.ts`'s `selection = []` default are **gone**; the `!user` label path is handled by `signalPlanFor({ signedIn, entitlementStatus, authLoading, … })` (`app/arena/page.tsx:344`); **`if (!res.ok || cancelled) return;` still appears twice in `app/arena/page.tsx`**, which is the member that leaves chart alerts at their last value. The other two were not re-checked. **So: 3 of 7 verified fixed, 1 verified still present, 3 unverified.** *(was #1347 item 11)*
- [x] **[PM 2026-11-08] DECIDED: WON'T UNIFY, and nobody should later.** They have different speakers: `lib/grok.ts:1175` is the APP describing the trader to the model (third person, plus instruction lines), while `app/(main)/arena/page.tsx:1746` is pre-filled into the chat INPUT for the trader to send (`prefillOnly`, `GrokChat.tsx:522` setInput), so first person is correct. `describeSelection` already owns the indicator names for both, which was the part that needed one definition (Dev, 2026-11-08). **[PM 2026-11-08] NARROWED to the two PROMPT sentences** (`lib/grok.ts:1175` and `app/(main)/arena/page.tsx:1746`). The EMASignal.tsx line is user-facing UI and stays. Low priority. **Four surfaces still write four different carrier sentences — now three, and the helper exists to prevent exactly this.** Live today: `app/arena/page.tsx:1598` *"The trader has chosen to weigh these indicators"*, `app/arena/page.tsx:1742` *"I am weighing these indicators"* (first person), `components/EMASignal.tsx:218` *"Your selection (…) changed this call"*. GrokChat's own sentence is gone. `describeSelection` (`lib/strategyRegistry.ts`) correctly owns the name list for all call sites; only the surrounding sentence drifts. Low severity. *(was #1347 item 16)*

## Done and shipped (kept for the record)

- [x] **Locked coin says "available in Pro"** and names what Free still includes — live, `v2026.10.21`. *(was #1609, closed 2026-10-23)*
- [x] **A pending Buy/Sell marker draws solid**, like a confirmed one — live, `v2026.10.22.2`, owner-approved. *(was part of #1673)*
- [x] **Open-interest trend uses one 60-minute window** on every surface — live, verified against both venues. *(was #1613 / #1617)*

## Rules for this tracker

- **New Arena findings get a checkbox here, not a new issue.** That is the point of it.
- A checkbox ticks only when the close rule is met: QA tested, QA audited, it passed manual testing, PM audited, **and the owner approved it if it is visual.**
- Anything genuinely not Arena goes elsewhere — this does not become a dumping ground.








- [x] **4.1.2 half FIXED and verified on production 2026-11-10:** `category-chips-aria-pressed` passed 2/2 (desktop and mobile, real durations) against prod `fab41aa` (QA, #2097 prod re-check). The 1.4.1 colour-only half is parked below. Original: **Coin category selection is signalled by colour alone.** `aria-selected`, `aria-checked` and `aria-pressed` are all null on all five chips, and font-weight is 700 either way, so a screen-reader user gets no indication of the active category (QA, qa, 2026-11-08). Fix: `aria-pressed` on `.gsc-tf-btn`. Priority: medium (WCAG 4.1.2). (Added by PM.)




- **PARKED (post-launch, owner's option A, 2026-11-10):** **Coin category chips still show selection by COLOUR ALONE (WCAG 1.4.1).** QA measured the CSS 2026-11-10: `.gsc-tf-btn.on` changes only `background`, `color` and `border-color`; `font-weight` (700) and border width (0.5px) are the same in both states. #2071 / `4d396e41` fixed **4.1.2** (screen readers now announce the pressed state), not 1.4.1, and says so ("No visual change"). A user who can't tell the purple from the grey still can't see which category is active. Fix: one non-colour cue (weight, underline, check mark or border width). Visual, so PM verifies per the 2026-11-06 waiver. Same class as #1185's parked aria-pressed sweep (51 toggles in 18 files). (Added by PM, from QA's measurement.)




- [x] **Arena's own deep link accepts only the ~50 core coins, though Arena now offers 463.** `/arena?coin=cyber` (or `xaut`, `gram`) silently loads **BTC** and rewrites the URL. The cause is `arena/page.tsx:234-235`, which validates the param against `COINS` (core), not the universe. **In-app links are unaffected**, because Briefing, Dashboard and Markets only link core coins. **What breaks:** a shared link or a **reload** while viewing a non-core coin lands on BTC with no message. Not new vs production (core-only there too). Found by QA on `b62d9c0`, 2026-11-11: three coin names, one identical VWAP `$73,768.50`, which is BTC's. Priority: medium. Next release. (Added by PM.)

- [x] *(PM 2026-11-14: closed on QA evidence 6870071227 on deployed qa: 1W and 1M timeframes exist (#2157); BTC 1W loads 347 candles back to 2020-03, 1M 81 back to 2020-03, HYPE 1M 24, i.e. years of history on first load. Panning added no further candles because the whole history is already loaded; #2132 scroll-back on short timeframes is not shown by this harness.)* **Owner request, 2026-11-12: weekly and monthly timeframes on the Arena chart, and years of history.** **History:** scroll-back (#2132, in release v2026.11.12, not yet live) pages older candles with no cap, until the venue returns nothing. Measured on qa 2026-11-12 08:3xZ: Binance spot has BTC daily before 2019-01-01, while **Bybit linear returns nothing before 2019-01-01**. So the depth depends on which venue the chart reads, which is about 5+ years for BTC on Bybit's perp history (to be confirmed by QA's scroll-1 row). **Timeframes:** the klines route already allowlists `1w` and `1M` for Binance and both answer on qa. Adding **1W and 1M to the chart toolbar** is chart-only scope; signals, AI read and Draw Structure stay on ≤1d unless decided otherwise. **6M and 1Y:** no venue offers them, so they would have to be built from monthly candles, and BTC has only about 6–8 yearly candles, too few for the EMA ribbon or RSI. **Owner decided 2026-11-12: Weekly + Monthly only (option A); 6M and 1Y are not to be built.** Priority: medium. Next release. (Added by PM.)


- [ ] **Strategy panel clean-up (owner, 2026-11-12: "very confusing... needs massive improvement").** **His decisions, first-hand to PM:** (1) **Pro and 14-day trial: unlimited indicators, no counter.** Today it's `LIMITS = { pro: 3, free: 1 }` (`lib/strategyRegistry.ts:265`), copied in September from a reference product, with no cost reason in the code. (2) **Free and signed-out: 1, with an upgrade prompt** instead of a silent refusal. (3) **A clean-up, not a redesign:** only indicators that draw are shown (#2112 already hides the unwired 12 on `qa`), plain words, chart layers split from indicators, the explanatory paragraph removed. **PM's design:** https://claude.ai/artifact/QfTSnmrvjykpGwGCTgQZXX (Pro dark interactive, Free dark interactive, Pro light, phone 390). The structure: `INDICATORS` (SMA, Parabolic SAR, MACD, Bollinger Bands as checkbox chips with a one-line plain description, a check mark as the non-colour cue, "N on"); `CHART LAYERS` (EMA ribbon, RSI pane, GEX "BTC only" as Always-on rows; S/R and Liquidation clusters as real switches synced with the chart toolbar); Free = single choice where tapping another swaps it, plus a persistent "Pro turns on every indicator together · See Pro" callout. **Dev must verify before building:** that the AI read really uses every selected indicator (the copy claims it), and that GEX is BTC-only. **Design APPROVED by the owner 2026-11-12.** **Plus his rule, same day: changing an indicator must update the chart's buy/sell signal live ("it also auto adjusts").** Today only SMA can change the call (`verdictChangedBySelection`, `lib/useEMAStrategy.ts:104-111`). RSI is advisory, and PSAR, MACD and Bollinger don't touch the markers. That falls short of his 2026-09-07 on-the-fly rule (#985). **Required:** every selectable indicator takes part. When the selection changes, the markers recompute immediately, a marker shows only where the selected indicators agree, and the chart says the signal is filtered by the trader's strategy. Telegram/push alerts stay on the base EMA rule (his 09-07 ruling, unchanged). Group 1. Priority: high. (Added by PM.)


- [x] *(PM 2026-11-14: closed on QA evidence 6867541588: cyber, xaut, gram, nvda open by link; unknown coin says so; runs 43454376715, 43446333285; scanner tokenized rows priced per #2245.)* **Owner order, 2026-11-12: "PUT ALL TOKENIZED STOCKS ON OUR PLATFORM"** (he asked why NVDA is missing). **Cause, measured by PM against live exchange APIs:** `scripts/generate-coins.mjs` keeps only USDT perps on **both** Bybit and Binance (`:208`), and requires Binance `contractType === 'PERPETUAL'` (`:173`). **Binance lists stock perps as `contractType: "TRADIFI_PERPETUAL"`** (NVDA, TSLA, AMZN, META, GOOGL, HOOD, MSTR, COIN…), so every one is dropped. Bybit lists them as ordinary `LinearPerpetual` (AAPL, AMZN, COIN, GOOGL, HOOD, META, MSFT, MSTR…). **Build:** accept `TRADIFI_PERPETUAL`, tag those rows `kind: 'stock'`, add a **Stocks** category chip in Arena, and give each one a plain label ("Tokenized stock") with a short note that the perp trades 24/7 while the underlying market keeps its own hours (data honesty: weekend prices move without the stock market open). Charts, scanner and OI work as for any universe coin. The AI read stays core-only, as for every non-core coin. Priority: **high** (owner order). (Added by PM.)






- [x] **Picking a strategy changes the CHART, not only the text (owner, first-hand, 2026-11-15).** He picked "Liquidity sweep + structure shift", got WAIT, and nothing on the chart changed. **His decisions:** ships in the **next** release (not release 2); the chart draws **the strategy's key levels plus markers**. Spec to Dev: an optional `overlay` on the strategy result (levels, zones, marker) computed from the same closed candles as the verdict; the levels the strategy is **watching** are drawn on WAIT too; on BUY/SELL, an arrow on the signal candle plus the invalidation line. Per strategy: sweep = swept swing + break level; EMA stack = 4 EMAs; VWAP = day VWAP; Bollinger = bands + marker; RSI divergence = line joining the two swings; supply/demand = zone box; NY open = open price + opening range. Main chart only, latest state only, redrawn on strategy/coin/timeframe change, no layout shift. Branch `feature/arena-strategy-chart-overlays`. Priority: high. (Added by PM.) **Verified (QA Team): shipped v2026.11.17 (#2409). Deployed qa build, group runs 44010875227 and 43991178908, cell F4: all nine strategies on a signed-in Pro account, the chart carries the strategy's label boxes and a WAIT call lists its watched levels; PM visual: yes (PM looked at the F4 shots).**

- [x] Overlay **label boxes are all the same blue**. The spec gives each role its colour (watch/confirm accent, "Wrong if" amber, reference neutral): the dashed lines follow it, the label boxes don't. Priority: low. (Added by PM.) **Verified (QA Team): shipped v2026.11.17 (#2409). Group runs 44010875227 and 43991178908, cell F4: label boxes take their role colours (checked per strategy); PM visual: yes (F4 shots).**
- [ ] Dashboard: the card title still asks **"IS NOW A GOOD TIME TO TRADE?"**, the scale reads "≥ 70 good", and the page hint says "the best setup right now… before you place a trade". These are the same advice framing the headline fix removed. Proposed: "HOW MANY SIGNALS AGREE", "≥ 70 most agree", and a hint that describes the page. Priority: medium (data integrity). (Added by PM.)
- [x] Strategy call box on WAIT: the reserved band still shows about 80 px of empty space under a short reason (the owner's earlier spacing note). Fill it with the levels the strategy is watching, in text (the overlay data already exists). Priority: medium. (Added by PM.) **Verified (QA Team): shipped v2026.11.17 (#2409). Group runs 44010875227 and 43991178908, cell F4: a WAIT call lists the watched levels as "Watching: <label> <price> · ..." (max 4, no empty line) for every strategy; PM visual: yes (F4 shots).**

**Owner, first-hand, 2026-11-17 (screenshot):** the Strategy panel indicator chips have "awful UX, not smooth": tapping feels slow and jumpy, the chips look cluttered, and the numbering should go ("no need for it"). PM's build spec went to Dev; it ships in the next release.
- [ ] **A tap must always toggle.** Today, with 2 or more indicators on, tapping an on chip only refocuses its parameters and does not deselect it (the #1027 rule), so the tap appears to do nothing. Parameter editing moves into the params box. Priority: high. (Added by PM.)
- [ ] **The chip flips instantly.** The selection update is deferred (optimistic pressed state + `startTransition`), and the chart and filter read a deferred value. Target: INP ≤ 100 ms at 4x CPU throttle, 390 px. Priority: high. (Added by PM.)
- [ ] **Nothing moves on a tap.** The params area is reserved, so CLS on a tap is 0. Priority: high. (Added by PM.)
- [ ] **Look:** no order numbers; a single 1px accent border when on (no extra inset ring); names never wrap; columns follow the container width (desktop rail = 1 column of compact rows, phone = 2 columns); equal row heights. Priority: medium. (Added by PM.)

**QA, 2026-11-17 (qa/staging 963f1e5; accepted for this release, next-release items). Signed: QA Team**
- [ ] **CLS, signed in, saved strategy, Russian, 360 px:** worst of 6 loads 0.125 (loads 0.104 to 0.125; budget 0.1). The 2026-11-16 production release measured 0.124, so this is unchanged. Largest shift sources: the right-rail "Market snapshot" and "Run the read" blocks (0.019 to 0.040 per entry), the "Спросить ИИ" launcher moving 704 to 525 px, the Indicators and Chart layers sections reflowing (about 0.024), and the plan area in the top bar widening. Every other state measured at or below 0.066. Run 43991045197. Priority: medium.
- [ ] **Supply and demand strategy:** the "Demand" label box sits on top of the Buy marker (visual review of run 43991178908). Priority: low.
- [ ] **"Saving…" toast** covers the S/R and Structure toolbar buttons for a moment (visual review of run 43991178908). Priority: low.



- [ ] **Strategy panel too tall (owner, first-hand 2026-11-17, screenshot): he has to scroll to adjust the strategy.** He chose "tighten everything": no blank band under the call (exact 3-line reservation, chevron for more), indicators 2x2 name-only chips, Pro note one line, chart layers as one caption + two side-by-side switches, tighter section spacing. Target: whole panel at most 560 px at a 360 px rail in en and ru; Run buttons visible at 1280x800 without scrolling; CLS unchanged. Priority: high. (Added by PM; build spec sent to Dev.)
- [ ] **Slow 3G (400 kbps, 400 ms RTT), /faq at 390 px:** DOM ready 11.7 s and LCP 11.8 s (audit matrix pilot, staging run 44074322126). Priority: low (performance); the full slow-network column is in the matrix shards.


### Owner request 2026-11-17: Channel strategy + risk box on Draw Structure (owner chose "Box, no arrow")
The owner showed a chart with a falling channel, support/resistance zones, a long position box (entry, stop, target, risk:reward 2.82) and a drawn predicted path, and asked for "this kind of analysis on the Arena page when the user clicks Draw Structure, and also as part of a strategy". Asked first-hand with options, he chose **the box without the predicted-path arrow**. This supersedes the 2026-10-31 rule in `lib/drawStructure.ts` ("no target, no entry"), and only for levels that come from a strategy's own rules.
- [ ] **New strategy "Channel" in the Strategy set** (same gating as the other strategies). Uses the existing channel detector on CLOSED candles (≥3 pivots per rail, the current fit thresholds). BUY = first close above the upper rail of a falling channel; SELL = first close below the lower rail of a rising channel; otherwise WAIT ("No close outside a channel yet."). Levels: Entry = the breakout candle's close; Stop = the last swing on the other side, inside the channel; Target = the nearest support/resistance zone in the trade's direction (the chart's own S/R). With no zone, no target and no R:R are shown. Verdict sentence of 12 words or fewer, describing what the candles did. Priority: high (owner). (Added by PM.)
- [ ] **Draw Structure shows the risk box.** When a channel is drawn and the Channel strategy has a live BUY/SELL call, draw the position box: green reward area from entry to target, red risk area from entry to stop, labels "Target", "Entry" and "Stop" with price and % distance, and "R:R 2.8". Also draw the S/R zones as bands. **No predicted path or arrow, ever.** One caption: "Levels from the Channel strategy, not a prediction." With no live call: channel and zones only, no box. Priority: high (owner). (Added by PM.)
- [ ] Phone (390): the box labels stay readable (short form "T / E / S"), and nothing covers the price axis. Light and dark. Priority: high. (Added by PM.)
- [ ] QA: synthetic falling-channel and rising-channel fixtures (breakout and no-breakout); R:R arithmetic; no box without a call; no arrow element anywhere; CLS of 0.1 or less when the box appears. (Added by PM.)


### Owner decision 2026-11-17: new strategies, "5 now, 2 next" (first-hand, clickable)
Source: a list the owner brought from a Google AI search. The PM checked each one against our 8 strategies and our data. Every strategy follows the existing rules: closed candles, the same gating, a verdict of 12 words or fewer that describes what happened, Entry/Stop/Target from the strategy's own rules (Target = the nearest S/R level in the trade's direction when no rule gives one; no target means no R:R), 5 locales, and QA fixtures with an oracle.

**Phase 1 (now):**
- [ ] **Golden / Death cross (EMA 50/200):** BUY = the 50 EMA closes above the 200 EMA; SELL = the reverse. Entry = the cross candle's close; Stop = the lowest low (BUY) or highest high (SELL) of the last 20 candles; Target = nearest S/R. WAIT: "No 50/200 cross on the latest closed candles." (Added by PM.)
- [ ] **S/R flip:** BUY = after a close above a resistance level, the first retest that touches the level and closes back above it; SELL = the reverse. Entry = the retest close; Stop = just beyond the level (or the retest wick); Target = the next S/R. (Added by PM.)
- [ ] **Range bounce:** uses the detector's flat range (3 or more touches each side). BUY = a touch of the range low that closes back inside; SELL = the same at the top. Entry = close; Stop = beyond the range edge; Target = the opposite edge. WAIT when there is no range or price is mid-range. (Added by PM.)
- [ ] **Fair value gap (FVG):** a bullish gap is when candle i-2's high is below candle i's low. BUY = the first return into an unfilled bullish gap that closes above the gap's bottom; SELL = the reverse. Entry = close; Stop = beyond the gap; Target = the recent swing or nearest S/R. (Added by PM.)
- [ ] **Asia / London session sweep:** Asia range 00:00–08:00 UTC, London 07:00–12:00 UTC (confirm the hours with Dev). BUY = a wick below the session low that closes back inside; SELL = the same above the high. Entry = close; Stop = beyond the sweep wick; Target = the opposite side of the session range. 5m to 1h. (Added by PM.)
- [ ] **Grouped dropdown:** Trend (EMA stack, Golden/Death cross) · Price action (Supply/demand retest, Liquidity sweep, S/R flip, Range bounce, FVG, Channel breakout, RSI divergence, BB squeeze) · Sessions (NY open, Asia/London sweep, VWAP reclaim) · Derivatives (phase 2). Each option gets a one-line tooltip saying what data it uses. (Added by PM.)

**Phase 2 (next):**
- [ ] **Funding + OI squeeze:** a crowding condition (funding at an extreme, OI rising, a dense liquidation cluster nearby) plus a candle trigger (the first close through the last swing against the crowded side). Rules to be agreed with Dev before building; no "fade" wording. (Added by PM.)
- [ ] **CVD absorption:** price makes a lower low or higher high while aggressive flow (CVD) pushes the same way, and the candle closes back. Reuses the existing absorption detector. (Added by PM.)

Skipped or merged, with the reason: Trendline retest (part of Channel breakout); Fib OTE, HTF+LTF and Anchored VWAP (no clean closed-candle rule yet); GEX pin (BTC only).


### Owner decisions 2026-11-17: indicator settings (first-hand, clickable)
- [ ] **RSI (length, 70/30 lines) and EMA ribbon lengths become adjustable** under "Edit settings", with the existing SMA, MACD, SAR and Bollinger parameters. (Added by PM.)
- [ ] **The AI read (Quick, Deep, Ask) uses each trader's saved indicator settings** for the indicators they have turned on. Values are computed server-side with the user's parameters and stated with their settings ("RSI(21) = 38.2"). **Strategy BUY/SELL/WAIT signals keep their standard rules.** Panel note: "The AI read uses your settings. Strategy signals use standard settings." The AI-read sanity check (#2502) compares against the same values. (Added by PM.)

- [ ] **Owner-reported 2026-11-17 (production, Free account, HYPE 30m):** the Strategy panel's run row QUICK / DEEP / ASK AI shows unlocked (QUICK filled gold), while the top "Quick Research" / "Deep Research" buttons show the lock because the coin is not on the Free list. That is confusing. Fix in #2500: the run row uses the same gating as the top buttons (lock icon, locked style, same upgrade prompt), and the same applies to the used-up allowance and plan-checking states. ASK AI follows "Ask LiquidityAI". Priority: high. (Added by PM.)

- [ ] **Owner-reported 2026-11-17: VWAP "Unavailable" on HYPE (production).** Measured by PM: `/api/market/snapshot` `klines` returns 49 coins and HYPE is missing (PEPE and BONK are present), and the client never fetches HYPE's 15m klines either. So VWAP, RSI14, POC/VAH/VAL and MA20 are all missing for HYPE. Fix: per-coin fallback to Bybit klines when Binance has nothing. Priority: high (data integrity). (Added by PM.)
- [ ] **Owner gating rule 2026-11-17:** the S/R and Liquidation-cluster chart layers are free only on BTC, ETH and SOL; on every other coin they are Pro (lock on the chip, the same upgrade prompt). The EMA and RSI layers stay free. (Added by PM.)
- [ ] **Owner + PM 2026-11-17: too many upsell texts on /arena.** Measured on production, Free account, HYPE: 10 upsell strings on one screen ("· UPGRADE", 4× "Upgrade", "Signals for this coin are Pro only.", "Want more than one at once? … See Pro", "PRO FEATURE", "Unlock with Pro"). Target 3 or fewer per screen: keep the header Upgrade; locked controls get a lock icon that opens one shared upgrade sheet; one short "· Pro" line per locked section, with no extra buttons; one wording ("Pro") everywhere. Priority: medium. (Added by PM.)

### Onyx keys and types - `ONYXKEYS.TRANSACTIONS_PENDING_FRAUD_REVIEW = 'transactionsPendingFraudReview'` and `ONYXKEYS.LOCALLY_PROCESSED_FRAUD_TRANSACTION_REVIEWS` (client-only, so a device doesn't re-prompt for a review it already actioned), next to their 3DS siblings. - 3DS challenges expire after minutes, so it’s fine to permanently suppress a 3DS review if we failed to process it. Since fraud reviews don’t expire, we’ll store a timestamp instead of a boolean in `LOCALLY_PROCESSED_FRAUD_TRANSACTION_REVIEWS`, so if we failed to record the feedback for some reason, we can re-surface the review after some time has passed - `type TransactionPendingFraudReview` as `Omit` ### Forced review navigation Expand [useNavigateTo3DSAuthorizationChallenge](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/a733d2301920701dd756b1f21205e88f3907f3a0/src/libs/Navigation/useNavigateTo3DSAuthorizationChallenge.ts) to a more generic `useNavigateToForcedTransactionReview` - `ThreeDSAuthHandler` becomes `ForcedTransactionReviewHandler` - `useNavigateToForcedTransactionReview`’s `transactionPending3DSReview` becomes `transactionsPendingReview`, sorted and synthesized from both onyx queues - Items in `LOCALLY_PROCESSED_FRAUD_TRANSACTION_REVIEWS` will only be ignored from the queue within a week of their timestamp - 3DS takes precedence when both queues have entries (3DS requests expire in minutes; fraud reviews don't expire) - The hook’s existing behavior is what we want here. It watches the list, and every time a review arrives or is removed, it: - Picks the most pressing transaction - Double-checks freshness via GetTransactionsPendingFraudReview - Ensures the user isn’t already in the middle of a review flow - Force-navigates to the review route - When multiple reviews are pending, the user resolves them one at a time. ### The review screen Implement a new `ReviewTransactionPage` cloned from [AuthorizeTransactionPage](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/a733d2301920701dd756b1f21205e88f3907f3a0/src/pages/MultifactorAuthentication/AuthorizeTransactionPage/index.tsx), registered in the `MultifactorAuthenticationStackNavigator `so it presents full-screen on mobile and as the right-hand panel on web - Route `multifactor-authentication/review-transaction/:transactionID`; content per the mocks (amount, merchant, card, "Do you recognize this transaction?"), buttons "Yes, I do" / "No, it wasn't me". - Navigation interception comes from a new shared hook, `useForcedReviewScreen`, extracted from `AuthorizeTransactionPage` without behavior changes. It owns the four pieces of lifecycle logic that are identical across both screens and are the easiest to get subtly wrong: - The allowNavigatingAway ref and the useBeforeRemove [intercept](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/467ae4c879e54666dbb570f9e6f3f8d3dce68912/src/pages/MultifactorAuthentication/AuthorizeTransactionPage/index.tsx#L82-L90) that turns a back-press into the confirmation drawer. - The [offline branch](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/467ae4c879e54666dbb570f9e6f3f8d3dce68912/src/pages/MultifactorAuthentication/AuthorizeTransactionPage/index.tsx#L66-L76) — FullPageOfflineBlockingView does not wrap HeaderWithBackButton, so back-navigation while offline must bypass the drawer and dismiss directly. - The auto-dismiss [effect](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/467ae4c879e54666dbb570f9e6f3f8d3dce68912/src/pages/MultifactorAuthentication/AuthorizeTransactionPage/index.tsx#L130-L138) when the transaction disappears from Onyx (actioned on another device), suppressed while a submit is in flight or an outcome screen is showing. - The transient "transaction is already gone but the request has not resolved" [state](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/467ae4c879e54666dbb570f9e6f3f8d3dce68912/src/pages/MultifactorAuthentication/AuthorizeTransactionPage/index.tsx#L144-L165), which must render a spinner rather than dismissing. - Outcome screens per the mocks: recognized → "Retry your purchase within 10 minutes and it will go through"; not recognized → the frozen-card confirmation, deep-linking to the card page, which already renders the frozen state with the card-scarf illustration and Unfreeze CTA. #### Review Outcome Screens - Implement new Try Again, Frozen Card, and Card Terminated success outcome screens with createScreenWithDefaults - If RecordFraudFeedback reports that a transaction has already been reviewed, we will always show a dedicated “Already reviewed on a different device” failure screen - Implement other relevant edge case failure screens ### MFA scenario and actions - New scenario `RecordFraudFeedback` cloned from [AuthorizeTransaction](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/a733d2301920701dd756b1f21205e88f3907f3a0/src/components/MultifactorAuthentication/config/scenarios/AuthorizeTransaction.tsx): allowedAuthenticationMethods: [BIOMETRICS_HSM, PASSKEYS], action = the recognized-path API call. The existing orchestrator handles enrollment (magic code → key registration) for users who never set up biometrics/passkeys — no new enrollment work. - New actions in `src/libs/actions/MultifactorAuthentication/`: - `recordFraudFeedbackRecognized` (through the scenario, sends signedChallenge + authenticationMethod) - `recordFraudFeedbackNotRecognized` + a fireAndForget variant for the back-out path (no MFA, mirroring [denyTransaction](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/a733d2301920701dd756b1f21205e88f3907f3a0/src/libs/actions/MultifactorAuthentication/index.ts)). - All use `makeRequestWithSideEffects`, optimistically update `LOCALLY_PROCESSED_FRAUD_TRANSACTION_REVIEWS`, and map backend messages ("Transaction already reviewed") to outcome screens via the existing `API_RESPONSE_MAP` pattern.

raw.body:
**North star.** AGK: the AI delivery platform. People decide. AI builds. Every change is proven. A problem in a person's words takes one guided path, in every work type and every mode, to a delivered product that stays on course; the owner only answers questions and says yes or no.

**How this plan is read.** Eight phases, each with: what is built on the default branch today, what is drafted (a spec waiting for an approval), the builds still to run, and the gaps and edge cases closed by them. Then the cross-cutting foundations, the human decisions the plan needs, the waves in which builders run around the clock, and the done rule. Every build below is one brief, tests first, about 300 lines, from the default branch, through the ordinary gates; nothing here changes the hold list (spec approvals, `constitution/`, reviewers, ruleset, workflows, releases stay with the owner).

## Phase 1: the front door (the entry)
- Built: `/agk:vision` (SPEC-0029), `/agk:spec` intake (SPEC-0012), `/agk:brief`, solo and personal mode (SPEC-0041), the data guard (SPEC-0042).
- Drafted: SPEC-0048 (#655, intake REQ-055): a problem issue (`agk-problem`, `Problem: <words>`) or `/agk:vision` both start the same path; `front_door.py check-issue`.
- Builds: 0048 (b) the entry and the discovery document.
- Gaps closed: a problem arriving as an issue, in any mode; a problem longer than the limit (refused naming the rule, never the words); a problem that is really a bug (routes to SPEC-0046, not discovery); two problems with the same slug (slug rule refuses the second).

## Phase 2: discovery (the questions that matter)
- Built: the ten common questions of `engines.py` (SPEC-0029).
- Drafted: SPEC-0048 rules 4 and 5: the kit's ten plus the playbook's `[[discovery]]` questions, each asked once; one discovery document per problem; no session answers a question.
- Builds: 0048 (c) the discovery questions and amendment 130; 0048 (f) the auto-pilot drive (`Discovery: round <n>`, the conductor asks, the owner answers, no mode skips a phase).
- Gaps closed: an unanswered question stalls only its own phase (the rest of the plan proceeds); a changed answer re-opens the design, never the builds already merged; discovery in auto-pilot still waits for a person on every answer.

## Phase 3: research (sourced options)
- Built: the pilot research gate (SPEC-0038 rule 10, for `pilot` only).
- Drafted: SPEC-0048 rule 6: `docs/research/<slug>.md` for every work type, sources dated, the 180-day freshness rule.
- Builds: 0048 (d) the research record and `check-research`; stack detection for an existing repository (new brief: `front_door.py detect` reads the lockfiles and manifests and proposes the work type and stack, never decides them).
- Gaps closed: a record older than 180 days blocks the go until refreshed; a source without a date is refused; research never runs in a check (no network in checks, rule 16).

## Phase 4: design (prototype or demo, then the go)
- Built: SPEC-0037 design phase (rules 1, 2, 4, 6 merged in #365's builds); SPEC-0029 stack ADR.
- Drafted: SPEC-0048 rules 7 to 9: one review artifact fitted to the kind (screens: a click-through prototype; no screens: `Demo:` or `Walkthrough:`); the go is one line by a listed approver on the PR that carries the artifact.
- Builds: 0048 (e) the artifacts without screens; the parked SPEC-0037 briefs #458 to #461 (check_design, the design approve line, the Screens line, design_compare); 0048 (h) the skills a playbook names.
- Gaps closed: a product with no UI still has a reviewable artifact; a prototype changed after the go needs a new go (the frozen version rule of #459); the go in auto-pilot is still a person's line.

## Phase 5: specs and the plan (one line to approve)
- Built: intake (SPEC-0012), approvals that survive unchanged spec text (#629), calibrated plan ranges (SPEC-0043), briefs by capacity and overlap (SPEC-0034), the ADR and amendment ladder.
- Drafted: SPEC-0048 rules 10 and 11: milestones from the playbook shape and the accepted stack; then the existing path, unchanged.
- Builds: SPEC-0038 (f) `/agk:brief` split by playbook kinds; (g) `session.py plan` lanes; (e) `/agk:stack` reads the playbook; requirement status by evidence (new brief: a check flips `planned` to `done` only when its proof passes and flags a `done` whose proof fails; today 35 requirements read `planned` while built).
- Gaps closed: a brief that touches a protected class without a reserved ADR is flagged at filing (#482); a spec approval given at one head stays valid while the text is unchanged (done, #629); two briefs that overlap on `Touches:` never run together (parallel safety, item 3, new intake).

## Phase 6: builds (the AI workforce)
- Built: conductor and builders (SPEC-0030, 0034), the guarded merge (SPEC-0039), pre-merge combined check (#616), batched main checks (#622), heavy-run queue (SPEC-0040), fail-closed secret scan (#640), model per kind of work (SPEC-0045 a, b), the failure issue and fix record (SPEC-0046 a, b), the rule budget (#648), conductor watch and sweep (#644), lessons (#646), mypy ratchet (#637).
- In flight: parallel workers (#642), SPEC-0038 (b) declaration (#653) and (c) web-app (#652).
- Builds: the pre-merge check runs the kit budget and map tests (new brief, SPEC-0039 amendment: closes the green-alone, red-together class seen twice today, #657 and #659); cost and time caps per build (item 1, new intake: a brief declares its budget, the conductor stops a builder that exceeds it and files the overrun as a lesson); builder liveness (#490); SPEC-0045 (c) the usage line read by the scorecard; the merge queue command (#643 build (b)); flaky quarantine (strategy decision 2, new brief); pinned CI tools (strategy decision 4, needs the owner's workflow yes).
- Gaps closed: a builder that dies before pushing is noticed within one sweep (today it is noticed when a person asks); a builder that loops is stopped by its cap; two PRs that are each green but red together never reach main; a flaky test is quarantined with an issue, never deleted.

## Phase 7: delivery (accepted against the goals)
- Built: the weekly product report (SPEC-0011, 0014 to 0026), the decision inbox, per-PR metrics, the pipeline document (SPEC-0036), releases by tag.
- Builds: product-owner acceptance loop (new intake: each goal of the discovery document is accepted by a listed person against its evidence; a release lists the goals it closes); the enterprise evidence pack per release (new intake: tests, scans, coverage, SBOM, decisions, in one folder named by tag); supply-chain security and SBOM (strategy item, new intake); runbooks (fold into SPEC-0047 or one brief).
- Gaps closed: a release cannot close a goal without its evidence; a tag that is not a release is caught (#433, #476 class) by the pack check; a report week with no merges still answers the five questions.

## Phase 8: stays on course (measured, learning, never outdated)
- Built: drift audit (SPEC-0004), unused code and coverage (#593 line, on), catch log and lessons ladder (#605, #646), rule budget (#648), guard ladder promotion by evidence (#646).
- Drafted: SPEC-0047 (#649 intake, re-fired today): the weekly scorecard with thresholds, trend and freshness.
- Builds: SPEC-0047 builds after approval; playbook freshness (amendment 129, the dated `reviewed` key; a playbook older than its window is flagged by the scorecard, never silently used); rule promotion monthly (each `rule` row revisited, #646 output); provider resilience (new intake: a second model provider for a kind of work, chosen by the `[models]` table); fleet view across projects, counts only (later).
- Gaps closed: a quiet drift (more rules, slower tests, lower coverage, older playbooks) crosses a threshold and opens an issue the same week; AGK in usage-only mode still measures itself (the scorecard runs from the kit, not from AGK's own repository).

## Cross-cutting foundations (already decided, owner yes 2026-11-06)
- Speed: parallel workers (#642), batched main checks (done), budget tests before merge, main check under 10 minutes (target in #631).
- Quality: tests first everywhere, the combined pre-merge check, the rule budget that only shrinks, the guard ladder, the mypy ratchet, flaky quarantine.
- Cost: the right model per kind (done), cost and time caps per build (item 1), usage in every Report (done), the scorecard's cost column.
- Security and privacy: the data guard at every step (SPEC-0042), mandatory secret scan (#640), no pilot data in AGK, evidence only for open failures and deleted on pass (SPEC-0046).
- Any stack: playbooks as checked data with gates and dated claims (SPEC-0038), derived per engagement, promoted by evidence; the expert engineer is the model, AGK supplies the discipline.

## Edge cases the plan must survive (each is a test in its build)
1. The owner is away for days: every phase waits on exactly one named line; nothing else stalls; the sweep lists what waits (SPEC-0036).
2. Two builders touch the same map or index: the second merges main and reruns before ready (row 4) and the overlap check refuses the pair.
3. Main goes red: one failure issue, one fix PR with the record, merges held and resumed (done today twice; the budget-test gap closes it).
4. A playbook is outdated: flagged by date, derived anew for the engagement, promoted only with evidence.
5. A model provider is down or rate-limited: the kind of work falls back by the `[models]` table; a build never silently degrades its model.
6. A builder exceeds its budget: stopped, the partial branch kept, a lesson filed.
7. A spec changes after approval: the approval lapses by text, not by sha (done, #629).
8. A repository adopted mid-life (K2): stack detection proposes, discovery confirms, nothing of AGK lands in the product repository unless asked (SPEC-0041).
9. Pilot or customer data appears anywhere: the guard blocks it at the hook, the scan refuses the PR, the issue carries counts only.
10. A phase is skipped in auto-pilot: refused by rule 13; the conductor's step list is the same in every mode.

## Human decisions this plan needs (the hold list, one line each)
- `Approve: <sha> SPEC-0048` and `Maintainer answer:` for its Q points (after my review of #655).
- `Approve: <sha> SPEC-0047` and its Q points (when #649's PR is ready).
- `Approve: <sha> SPEC-0006` for #653 at its head (amendment 131).
- Yes or no to the workflow changes: pinned CI tools and pytest-xdist on main (strategy decision 4).
- Yes or no to a scheduled conductor: an hourly scheduled task that runs the sweep, fires the next briefs by capacity and reports, so the queue moves when this chat is closed (tokens are spent without a person watching; caps from item 1 bound it).
- Intake approvals, as each arrives: cost caps (item 1), parallel safety (item 3), product-owner acceptance, evidence pack and SBOM, provider resilience, stack detection, requirement status by evidence.

## Waves (builders run around the clock; the conductor merges one at a time)
- Wave 0, now: #640, #646, #642, #652, #653 merge; #655 and #649 intakes reviewed, approvals asked.
- Wave 1, filed today without new approvals: SPEC-0038 (d) rag-app, (e) stack, (f) brief split, (g) plan lanes, (h) evidence; the pre-merge budget tests; requirement status by evidence; builder liveness (#490); flaky quarantine; intakes for items 1 and 3.
- Wave 2, after SPEC-0048 approval: 0048 (b), (c), (d) in parallel, then (e), (f), (g), (h); the parked design briefs #458 to #461; stack detection.
- Wave 3, after SPEC-0047 approval: the scorecard builds; playbook freshness (amendment 129); SPEC-0045 (c); the remaining playbooks (i) to (n) with the pilot playbook last.
- Wave 4, after their intakes: acceptance loop, evidence pack and SBOM, provider resilience, runbooks, fleet view.

## Done rule
AGK v1 is done when one problem, written by the owner as an issue in a fresh repository, reaches a tagged release with its evidence pack through every phase above, in auto-pilot, with the owner typing only answers and approval lines, and the scorecard for that week shows every threshold met. That run is the acceptance test of this plan and is recorded as a run record, counts and timings only.

Tracker rules: the conductor updates this body as builds merge (one line per build, `merged #N`); the owner's decisions are recorded under the hold list as `yes <date>` or `no <date>`; nothing is marked done without the merged PR number.


## Timeline (GitHub milestones; the conductor moves an item only with its merged PR number)
| Milestone | Due | What must be merged | Gate from the owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wave 1: foundations, speed and the playbook builds | Sun 9 Nov | #640 #646 #642 #652 #653 #673; #662 to #672 | `Approve: SPEC-0048` on #655; yes/no on pinned CI tools |
| Wave 2: the front door (SPEC-0048) | Fri 13 Nov | 0048 builds (b) to (h); #458 to #461; stack detection | `Approve: SPEC-0049` and `SPEC-0050` when their intakes land |
| Wave 3: the scorecard and the playbook library | Fri 20 Nov | 0047 builds (b) to (e); playbooks (i) to (n); 0045 (c); amendment 129; caps and parallel-safety builds | yes on the drift-audit workflow step and `Approve: SPEC-0004` (amendment 128) |
| Wave 4: delivery and resilience | Fri 27 Nov | acceptance loop, evidence pack and SBOM, provider resilience, runbooks | the four intake approvals |
| v1 acceptance run | Fri 4 Dec | the done rule above, in auto-pilot; 0047 build (f) after four weekly runs | the problem issue, written by the owner |

Measured rate on 2026-11-06: 26 merges in one day with 6 to 8 builders; the plan assumes 10 a day to leave room for reviews, reds and approvals. Every brief carries a `phase:` label and a milestone; a milestone slips only with a line here saying why.


## Approvals ahead of the plan (owner direction 2026-11-06: take approvals ahead, keep builders on unblocked work)
Rule: every approval a wave needs is asked in one batch at the start of the wave before it, never one at a time when a builder is already waiting. A builder never waits on a person: the ready pool below always holds at least five briefs whose spec is Approved.
- Batch A (ask tonight): `Approve: SPEC-0048` and its Q points (after the fix list on #655); yes/no on the two workflow changes (pinned CI tools with a weekly update PR; the scorecard step and `actions: read` in the drift-audit workflow, with `Approve: SPEC-0004` for amendment 128); yes/no on a scheduled conductor; a second account in `spec_approvers` as a delegate when the owner is away.
- Batch B (wave 2 start): `Approve: SPEC-0049` (cost caps) and `SPEC-0050` (parallel safety) with their Q points; amendment 129 (playbook `reviewed` key); amendment 135 (flake rerun).
- Batch C (wave 3 start): the four wave-4 intakes (acceptance loop, evidence pack and SBOM, provider resilience, runbooks).
Ready pool (Approved specs, no approval needed): SPEC-0038 (d) to (h) and (i) to (n); SPEC-0037 #458 to #461; SPEC-0045 (c); SPEC-0047 (b) to (d); SPEC-0046 later builds; #667 to #670.


## Standing principle (owner, 2026-11-06, quoted as data)
"what ever decipline we are bringing here or solving in AGK developement, should be implemented for AGK when it works with new projects. Keep remember that." Every check, budget, log, command and agent file AGK uses on itself reaches a project through the kit or the plugin; the exceptions are listed with a reason and may only shrink (#680, the parity check). Each follow-up move is a brief under this plan.

## Owner decisions, batch A (2026-11-06, "Yes")
- Pinned CI test tools with a weekly update PR: yes. Filed as #698 (P0, ADR-0328): one pin file, pytest-xdist, the full suite on main in workers.
- The scorecard step and `actions: read` in the drift-audit workflow: yes (`Approve: SPEC-0004` for amendment 128 still asked at build (e)).
- A scheduled conductor: yes; set up with a fixed cap of 6 builders until #671's caps land.
- A delegate approver: waiting for an account name.


## Owner ruling 2026-11-06, the secret scan (quoted as data)
"Got scan mandate: Go ahead with best recommendation which can be helpful in real projects scope." Recommendation A taken: a cloud builder defers the scan to CI with one declared body line on builder branches; the CI scan on the exact head stays the mandatory merge gate. Brief #683, PR #684, ADR-0327. Builders' standing instructions carry the line.

milestone.title: Lean delivery workflow
milestone.description: Deterministic phase manager; one implementer and one reviewer per PR. Target <= $20, <= 3 agents, <= 2 rounds per merged PR.

raw.body:
## Outcome

The owner gets delivery from issue to merge that a deterministic phase manager drives, with agents used only for judgment: shaping, building, reviewing and fixing. It matters now because two stagely-pro sessions (9–11 Nov) used about half the weekly Max quota, about $1,400 at API rates. That's about $39, about 12 agents and 2.7 review rounds per merged PR. The cost went to process, not code: review fan-out ($380), waiting inside model turns ($94 of `/goal`-driven calls), orchestrator context ($235), refused shell commands (1,455) and failed `review-post` calls (211 of 398). The skill text itself cost about $7. Evidence is in the [redesign doc](https://claude.ai/artifact/NCCxg5ZU8qrsepnkrahdaK).

### Design

**Driver.** A CLI command, `drive`, run from the owner's Claude Code session on the desktop, is the phase manager. It reads GitHub state, makes every phase change in code and, when judgment is needed, returns one instruction: which agent to start (implementer or reviewer), its model and its brief file. The session only dispatches: it runs `drive`, starts the named agent, then runs `drive` again with the agent's hand-back. Waits on CI, review or merge happen inside `drive` as a background call. Nothing picks up work unless an owner session is open. The owner's unit of work is an epic: `drive <epic>` shapes it into slices if it has none, then delivers every slice in dependency order, running independent slices one after another or side by side, until the epic is delivered or a step needs the owner. `drive <issue>` delivers one issue. There is no watcher, launchd job or unattended run.

**Phases.** Each phase change happens in code and is driven by GitHub state. No agent orchestrates.

| Phase | Actor | Enters when | Leaves when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shape | One planner agent with the owner, once per epic | An approved epic has no slices | Slices exist, each one deliverable alone |
| Start | CLI (`drive`) | The owner names an issue, or runs `--next` in an open session | Claimed, branch and worktree made, card In Progress, brief written |
| Build | One implementer agent (Sonnet for R0/R1, Opus for R2) | Started | The change passes the project gate once |
| Open | CLI | Build reports done | PR open, risk computed, review requested |
| Review | One reviewer agent (Sonnet for R0/R1, Opus for R2) | PR head has no review | One review posted: `ready`, `fixes` or `owner` |
| Fix | The same implementer, resumed | Verdict `fixes` | Blocking findings fixed and pushed |
| Merge | CLI, or the owner when the risk label requires it | `ready`, CI green | Squash-merged; issue closed, card Done, worktree removed |

**Contracts.**
- The CLI is the only writer of labels, claims, rounds, risk, auto-merge, PR state and board columns. Every command is idempotent and prints one JSON line.
- Risk is estimated at Start from the issue's scope packet, which picks the implementer's model. At Open the CLI recomputes it from the diff; risk only rises, and a rise to R2 moves the reviewer to Opus.
- Agents get a brief file and return at most 5 lines. Details go to the PR or issue.
- Waits on CI, review or merge run as one blocking `drive` call in the background, never as repeated model turns.
- The risk label alone decides whether the owner is involved. It is computed from what the change touches (owner paths and labels are inputs to it), never from line count. Owner-only steps (a risk the owner must judge, a device check, a decision, the owner's merge) go to an owner queue and end the agent's turn.
- Review covers standards and spec in one pass. Only Blocker and Important findings block. Nits are recorded, never block, and collect for a retrospective sweep. Round 2 reads only the delta. A third blocking round goes to the owner.
- Agents run one plain command per Bash call, so worktree isolation accepts every call.
- No doctrine. No rule makes an agent invoke a skill because of the path it touches or the project's rule list (the `Doctrine` sections in agent rules, and `agent-review`'s "invoke the craft, design and UX skills the project's agent rules name"). Each agent definition preloads only the skills its role needs; any other skill loads on demand from its description.

**Removed.** Everything the `drive` flow makes unused is deleted, not left dormant. Review, fixes and merges run only because `drive` started them in the owner's session; no service, schedule or queue runs them.

| Area | Removed | Kept or moved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLI | `afk` and all its subcommands (`install`, `uninstall`, `watch`, `start`, `check`, `merge`, `end`, `runs`, `reap`, `supervise`, `finish`); `lib/afk-board.mjs`, `lib/afk-runs.mjs`, `lib/afk-watch.mjs` (about 1,460 lines) and their tests; `issue queue` | The PR-state logic (verdict at head, round, cap, ship-ready) moves into `status` and `drive` first |
| Skills | `afk` and its references (`worker-brief.md`, `setup.md`); `agent-review` as a scheduled pass, with its queue and "wake the runner" phases; AFK eligibility review in `refine`; scheduled runs in `explore` and `improve`; `afk-ready.md` and the AFK lane rules in `spec` | `refine`, `explore` and `improve` stay as skills the owner invokes |
| Labels and config | `lane:afk`, `lane:proposed`, `state:claimed`; the `afk` block and `reviewQueue` in `.agents/config.json` | `lane:owner`, `type:*`, `risk:*`, `review:owner` |
| Owner machine | The launchd watchers for skills and stagely-pro, their `afk-launch.mjs` launchers and `.worktrees/afk-watch` worktrees, removed once by a documented cleanup step | `skills-main-refresh`, which only updates plugins |

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An issue goes from Todo to merged with every phase change made by the CLI. Transcripts show no agent-run `gh` edits of labels, claims, board columns or auto-merge. <!-- workflow:criterion an-issue-goes-from-todo-to-merged-with-e -->
- [x] Each PR uses one implementer run, plus one resume per fix round, and one reviewer run per round. No agent spawns another agent. <!-- workflow:criterion each-pr-uses-one-implementer-run-plus-on -->
- [x] Given an approved epic, `drive <epic>` delivers it end to end: slices it if needed, delivers each slice in dependency order, and closes the epic, stopping only for owner steps. <!-- workflow:criterion given-an-approved-epic-drive-epic-delive -->
- [x] Work starts only from an open owner Claude Code session; no watcher or scheduled job picks it up. No session polls. A PR waiting on the owner appears in the owner queue with its reason and link, and no agent keeps running for it. <!-- workflow:criterion work-starts-only-from-an-open-owner-clau -->
- [x] Only Blocker and Important findings block. Round 2 reviews only the delta. A third blocking round goes to the owner. Nits on merged PRs can be listed for a sweep. <!-- workflow:criterion only-blocker-and-important-findings-bloc -->
- [x] Every CLI command succeeds from a worktree-isolated agent, including `review-post`, and a failed command never leaves a claim behind. <!-- workflow:criterion every-cli-command-succeeds-from-a-worktr -->
- [x] Nothing in the removal table remains in the library or on the owner's machine, and review runs without any service, schedule or queue. <!-- workflow:criterion nothing-in-the-removal-table-remains-in -->
- [x] No skill or agent rule in this library mandates a skill invocation by path or rule list, and each agent definition names the skills it preloads. <!-- workflow:criterion no-skill-or-agent-rule-in-this-library-m -->
- [x] Issues are scoped by the nature of the problem, with no line limit (#408). <!-- workflow:criterion issues-are-scoped-by-the-nature-of-the-p -->
- [ ] The next milestone in a consuming repo is measured from its transcripts at ≤ $20, ≤ 3 agents and ≤ 2 review rounds per merged PR, and < 0.1 refused commands per agent. If it misses, the gap and its cause are recorded. <!-- workflow:criterion the-next-milestone-in-a-consuming-repo-i -->

### Non-goals

- Changing what the review checks (the standards and spec checklists).
- Changing `release`, `milestone` or `health` beyond replacing their `gh` recipes with CLI commands.
- Unattended delivery (the AFK factory). It comes back only after attended delivery works well, as its own epic, rebuilt on `drive` rather than restored from the removed code.
- New paid services, or changes to the GitHub identities (implementer bot, reviewer bot, owner).

### Decisions

- 2026-11-11: Nits are recorded but never block; merged PRs' Nits are swept retrospectively now and then (owner, project thread).
- 2026-11-11: One review mode; no separate author and team passes (owner).
- 2026-11-11: A deterministic process manages phases. No tokens go on phase management: no orchestrator agent and no `/goal` on delivery (owner).
- 2026-11-11: Size follows the nature of the problem. There is no line limit; an engine refactor or a global rename is one PR (owner; #408).
- 2026-11-11: Establish this spec before any rollout (owner). Approved the same day (owner).
- 2026-11-11: Only the risk factor decides whether the owner is involved. The number of lines never matters, so the `ownerLines` rule goes (owner).
- 2026-11-11: Models follow risk. The implementer and reviewer run Sonnet for R0 and R1 and Opus for R2 (owner).
- 2026-11-11: Remove the watcher. Delivery is driven from the owner's Claude Code session on the desktop, with no automatic pickup without one. The AFK factory follows only once this works well (owner).
- 2026-11-11: Remove the doctrine: no mandated, path-triggered skill invocations (owner).
- 2026-11-11: The owner works in epics: given an epic, the flow delivers it (owner).
- 2026-11-11: Clean up everything the refactor leaves unused, watchers included. Running review or anything else must not need a service; the session's `drive` flow manages it (owner).

### Open questions

None.

### Status

Approved by the owner on 2026-11-11. Slices #416-#421, #542, #556 and #557 and the shared refinement #551 are merged and closed; #408 is merged. The Reviewer's epic outcome comment (2026-11-16) judged eight criteria met; they are ticked. Open: #605 (transcript check, criterion `an-issue-goes-from-todo-to-merged-with-e`) and #606 (milestone measurement, criterion `the-next-milestone-in-a-consuming-repo-i`), both waiting on the stagely-pro#1611 milestone records. Next: #605 and #606.

labels.name: bounty

raw.body:
Capture for Gorgias, matching what `packages/zendesk-app` does in Zendesk: record what the AI drafted, what the human sent, and one-line reason, from inside the tool the expert already works in.

**Bounty: $100**, paid on merge (PayPal, Wise or GitHub Sponsors — your choice).

### What it should do

A Gorgias app (ticket sidebar widget) that, for a ticket with an AI draft in the reply box:

1. Detects a draft landing in the reply box and shows `Draft inserted · N words`.
2. Offers the reason picker (`reason_pack`, `support` codes by default) with an optional note.
3. On send, `POST /v1/capture` with `source: "gorgias"`, `externalId: "gr:<ticket id>"`, the ticket as `context`, and `draft` / `sent` as `{ text, fields? }`.
4. Honours `require_reason`.
5. Never blocks the send.

Gorgias ecommerce teams are the likely first users here, so the `support` reason pack and order-context fields matter more than the claims pack.

### Shape to follow

- `packages/zendesk-app/src/capture.ts` and its test are the reference; payload documented in [docs/capture.md](docs/capture.md).
- Land it as `packages/gorgias-app`, same build setup (`tsup`, `dist/*.zip` from `scripts/package.mjs`).
- Gorgias apps: https://developers.gorgias.com/docs/apps-overview
- TypeScript strict, no `any`. Unit tests for the payload builder required; a live Gorgias account is not.

### Out of scope

Gorgias's own stats, per-agent rates, reading a ticket with no draft in it.

Questions: comment here or shireen@overturn.run. Say in a comment that you are picking it up.

labels.name: bounty
labels.description: Paid external contribution; amount in the issue

raw.body:
Capture for Intercom, matching what `packages/zendesk-app` does in Zendesk: record what the AI drafted, what the human sent, and one-line reason, from inside the tool the expert already works in.

**Bounty: $100**, paid on merge (PayPal, Wise or GitHub Sponsors — your choice).

### What it should do

An Intercom app (Canvas Kit, inbox surface) that, for a conversation with an AI draft in the composer:

1. Detects a draft landing in the composer and shows `Draft inserted · N words`.
2. Offers the reason picker (`reason_pack`; `support` codes by default here) with an optional note.
3. On send, `POST /v1/capture` with `source: "intercom"`, `externalId: "ic:<conversation id>"`, the conversation as `context`, and `draft` / `sent` as `{ text, fields? }`.
4. Honours `require_reason`.
5. Never blocks the send.

Note that Intercom's Fin drafts and a human-written reply must be distinguishable: tag the run `draft:ai` only when the draft came from an assist, `draft:manual` when the human typed it. Guessing an origin we were not told is worse than `unknown`.

### Shape to follow

- `packages/zendesk-app/src/capture.ts` and its test are the reference; payload documented in [docs/capture.md](docs/capture.md).
- Land it as `packages/intercom-app`, same build setup (`tsup`, `dist/*.zip` from `scripts/package.mjs`).
- Canvas Kit: https://developers.intercom.com/docs/canvas-kit
- TypeScript strict, no `any`. Unit tests for the payload builder required; a live Intercom workspace is not.

### Out of scope

Intercom reporting, per-agent rates, reading a conversation with no draft in it.

Questions: comment here or shireen@overturn.run. Say in a comment that you are picking it up.

# Executive Program Director — P0 delivery blocker (not an architecture expansion)

**Outcome required:** The original Katie Developer Orchestrator (DO) tic-tac-toe project must autonomously commission a coding worker, implement the game, and reach independent Preview acceptance. The owner has explicitly rejected any workaround requiring manual browser-console JavaScript, token extraction, SQL or repeated sign-in. **Do not ask the owner to paste code or expose an access token.**

## Verified production state

- Repository: `mfackrell/katie`, production `https://katie-mu.vercel.app`.
- Original project `fe9d2658-41e3-44c1-ae8e-a0cba98371fe`, currently `paused`, phase `development`; 73/96 historical missions, zero coding packages, 13 nodes, 600000-token allowance, approved scope `4849dff2cfce136b3a1f3db675ee3cc8e6e84315aa3cc3700ca529dcd84fe6c6`.
- Owner explicitly authorized **only** deadline `2026-11-16T18:00:00Z` (Monday noon Central); renewal is not yet applied and original project cutoff remains `2026-11-15T18:00:00Z`. Source mission `62cd8da3-1bcc-41ae-9470-574c6b05e420`; old window `a837004e-75d3-497d-b05a-482886ed5a5f`; old continuation release `c1d9a5f1ac10396c3015a7d5ae5f22254502e5de`.
- PR #1053 merged at `c68548a02b6aaf64d446229e34347f0cbd939a67`. The reviewed `paused_expired_window_renewal` migration `20261115201337` and service-role-only SQL RPC `project_org_renew_paused_window` are installed. Current Vercel production observed READY at `68d6ae20b70d9cae992f1398ae3b56ada747644d` (unrelated later main commit).
- The exact approved recovery state hash was `7921e18f14755dc2395e0ead0e8faf8f67b5c92ae54b1686e6799f6b238d9bff`; revalidate against actual state before any action.
- There are **zero** `project_paused_window_renewals` receipts.
- Existing Katie conversation UI displays **Owner sign in (optional)** and an older **Authorize deadline and continue project** control. That older control in `components/director-recovery-control.tsx` invokes `renew_continue` or `recover_hierarchy`, **not** the narrowly approved `renew_paused_window` flow. The correctly constrained owner endpoint `POST /api/projects/organization` with `trialAction:renew_paused_window` verifies bearer with `verifiedProjectOwnerSession`, same-origin, exact deployed SHA, project/source/old window/scope/cutoff, and delegates to the guarded SQL RPC. It is **not connected to a first-party UI action**.
- Browser owner sign-in is user-reported active. External ChatGPT GitHub/Supabase connectors **cannot use the user's Katie browser session**, and must not bypass this boundary by direct SQL as a shortcut.

## Root product failure

The project is blocked at owner-authenticated renewal because the approved and deployed backend operation has **no usable first-party owner UI path or durably delegated owner-authorized continuation**. Asking the user to run JavaScript in browser DevTools or manually call SQL is unacceptable; it negates the purpose of DO. Fix the **product orchestration seam**, not the security guard.

## Engineering mandate — existing Runtime Recovery Engineer

**Troubleshoot first.** Determine the smallest safe existing-UI or server-side approach that uses the owner's **real authenticated Katie session** to record the exact, already-approved one-time renewal. Do **not** infer that the external ChatGPT conversation itself is an authenticated Katie user identity. Prefer enhancing the existing project recovery/Control Center so the owner simply uses a proper, clearly labeled control, or an already-existing authenticated approval can be durably consumed if independently verified in Katie. After the one legitimate authorization, the system must transition to automatic guarded execution rather than require manual API/SQL steps.

Acceptance:
1. The TTT project page presents the **correct one-time owner renewal** for `renew_paused_window` (or a verified preexisting durable owner authorization triggers it) with exact approved deadline `2026-11-16T18:00:00Z`. Do not use the obsolete `renew_continue`/hierarchy recovery path for this paused-project case.
2. Use existing `ownerSessionBearer()` and verified `POST /api/projects/organization` authentication (same-origin, current prod SHA). No token display, localStorage scraping, arbitrary owner grant, unauthenticated automation, or bypass of `verifiedProjectOwnerSession`.
3. Verify returned renewal receipt and unchanged `paused` status, 13-node contracts, scope, history, 96/600000 limits. Initiate only the separately guarded `project_org_resume_management` under the same authentic owner authorization or an explicitly recorded auditable delegation; fail closed and remain paused on mismatch. A resume may need a narrowly scoped owner endpoint; do not silently widen project controls.
4. After legitimate owner approval/recovery, **scheduler autonomously commissions a real coding package** through the preserved hierarchy. No manual coding, synthetic management decisions or new project. Monitor repeat management loops and preserve remaining budget.
5. Add deterministic owner-session/UI tests, browser acceptance and native PostgreSQL regression against the current production baseline, plus security and replay/expired-authority negatives. Preserve PR #1053 renewal/PR #1049 management-loop behavior, QA separation and source authorization.
6. If any engineering changes are necessary, prepare one narrowly scoped PR; no direct production change or live provider work. Independent QA sign-off and exact-tree CI required.

**Deadline urgency:** Owner's authorized new deadline is November 16, 2026 noon Central. Do not silently extend it or spend after expiration. If the required qualification cannot complete within it, clearly escalate rather than bypass.

**External EPD role:** Direct and verify; do not implement game manually. No further planning layers, broad continuity redesign, or new approvals except the actual existing owner security control.
